laurĕātus , a, um, adj. laurea,
I.crowned or decked with laurel, laureate: “imago,” Cic. Mur. 41, 88 : “lictores,” id. Att. 7, 10, 1 : “fasces,” id. Div. 1, 28, 59 : “legiones,” Liv. 45, 39 : litterae, a letter announcing a victory (so called because bound up with bay-leaves), a laurelled letter, id. 45, 1: “litterae a Postumio laureatae sequuntur,” id. 5, 28 fin. : “tabellae,” id. 45, 1 .—Subst.: laurĕātae , ārum (sc. litterae), a letter announcing a
victory: “ne laureatis quidem gesta prosecutus est,” Tac. Agr. 18 fin. ; cf. laurus.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
